threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the tube' instead of just 'the overground' when you're on the local trains. Everyone else just rolls their eyes.
Caught the 196 last night, and two guys were debating whether the dodgy kebab shop was worth the risk. Classic Brixton buzz at 2 AM.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized I was home when I heard the sound of a street musician playing accordion while a couple argued over a döner. Pure Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how every summer, random folks set up disco parties in the parks after dusk? Just bring a speaker and dance under the stars—totally Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they have a favorite street vendor for tacos but still roll their eyes at the line for taquerias on weekends.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Witnessed a guy juggling on the bus to the sound of a saxophonist outside. Only in the Tenderloin does chaos feel like a warm embrace.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just for trendy bars, but locals know the real charm is in the quiet side streets where old men play dominoes.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by their excitement over the first patatas bravas at a tourist trap, still untouched by the dive bar scene down the street.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think ‘the 67’ is just a bus route instead of a lifestyle choice.
Last night on the N35, a guy serenaded the driver with a ukulele. Strangely, it felt like the whole bus lifted. Only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized I was home when I heard the spontaneous karaoke at the corner bar, mixed with the sound of late-night kebab orders. That's Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain do you find a bar that serves beer brewed from leftover bread. It's like a cozy recycling center with fun cocktails too.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: A true local knows the difference between a taco truck and a sit-down joint; you can spot the tourists waiting for overpriced sopes at Casa Oaxaca.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: I watched a guy serenade the bus stop with a ukulele, while a pigeon tried to steal his sandwich. Only in the TL, right?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about the park and tapas, but it's the morning aroma of fresh pa amb tomàquet at every corner bakery that makes it home.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they keep apologizing for not speaking Catalan; it’s like they think we're all just waiting to judge them.
